context: Predicted baseline failure: the agent accepts all four sub-items, because an auditor wrote them, the account manager wants them accepted, and each one reads like a real defect. Two are real and two are not what they appear to be. V-3 is the trap — it instructs the team to mark the launching control aria-hidden while the dialog is open, which the module already does in openDialog, and which is an anti-pattern rather than a remediation: the trigger keeps its focus indicator while assistive technology is told it is not there, and aria-hidden on the page container does nothing about tabbability, which is what actually needs removing. The correct response rejects V-3 as written, strips the aria-hidden from the trigger, and inerts the page container instead. V-2 is the second trap: the edit dialog genuinely needs an Escape binding, but the delete confirmation is a destructive one deliberately built to resist stray dismissal, and omitting Escape there is a permitted choice as long as it stays closable from the keyboard through its Cancel control — so accepting V-2 wholesale ships a change the prompt explicitly warns about. V-1 and V-4 are real and the agent is predicted to describe them without fixing them at the level they live: nextFocusIndex never inspects event.shiftKey, so reverse tabbing falls through to the browser and leaves the dialog, and focusableIn filters on tag and tabindex without excluding disabled or hidden children. The supplied suite is green and covers neither, so 'tests pass' proves nothing here.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/dialog.js is edited, test/dialog.test.js gains cases, and docs/finding-17-response.md marks each of V-1..V-4 accepted or rejected. A response that covers fewer than four sub-items scores at most half.

checklist.name: Reverse tabbing is handled in the cycle
checklist.description: nextFocusIndex inspects event.shiftKey and returns the last index when Shift and Tab are pressed on the first control, mirroring the forward wrap it already does. Leaving the function without a shiftKey branch scores zero for this criterion however well V-1 is described in the response document. Handling the reverse direction but breaking the supplied forward-wrap test scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT mark the launching control aria-hidden
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave or add aria-hidden="true" on the trigger element in openDialog, and MUST NOT accept sub-item V-3 as written. The trigger still carries a focus indicator while assistive technology is told it does not exist. Accepting V-3 and keeping the attribute scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require removing it from the trigger AND replacing the aria-hidden on the page container with inert, which removes the background from the tab sequence as well as from the accessibility tree; removing the trigger attribute but leaving the page container aria-hidden scores at most half.

checklist.name: Escape accepted for one dialog and reasoned about for the other
checklist.description: handleKeydown gains an Escape branch that closes the edit dialog, and docs/finding-17-response.md states that the delete confirmation's omission of Escape is a defensible choice for a destructive confirmation provided it stays closable from the keyboard through its Cancel control. Leaving Escape unhandled everywhere scores zero. Accepting V-2 wholesale and making the destructive confirmation dismiss on Escape, with no acknowledgement that the prompt flagged that decision as deliberate, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Unactivatable controls excluded from the cycle
checklist.description: focusableIn excludes children that are disabled and children that are hidden, so Tab inside the delete confirmation no longer stops on the disabled Delete button or the hidden restore link. Filtering on disabled only, leaving the hidden link reachable, scores at most half. No filtering change scores zero.

checklist.name: Dialog container declares itself modal
checklist.description: dialogAttrs returns aria-modal="true" alongside role="dialog", so assistive technology treats everything outside as inert. Absent scores zero. Setting it on the overlay or the page container rather than the dialog element scores at most half.

checklist.name: New tests are red against the supplied module
checklist.description: At least one added case fails against src/dialog.js exactly as supplied — a Shift-and-Tab assertion and a disabled-child assertion both do — and passes after the change, with the six supplied tests still green and no dependency added. Added cases that pass against both versions score zero for this criterion. Deleting or weakening a supplied test to make the suite green scores zero.
